newsitem.title: MEXICO: Recovery forecast helping Cifra in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Recovery forecast helping Cifra in Q2.

text.p: Retailer Cifra SA's second quarter revenues and earnings will reflect the fledgling recovery in domestic consumption, analysts said.
For the first time since the 1994-95 economic crisis, the company could post positive results in store sales, they said.

"We are going to see very solid results, the first positive numbers in stores sales.... I think that the latest macroeconomic numbers will back up the recovery that we have already seen in real salaries and in manufacturing," said Sebastian Barry Taylor, an analyst with ING Barings.
Analysts said they expected revenues of 6.378 billion pesos in the second quarter, compared to 5.854 billion pesos in the same period in 1996.
They forecast per share earnings will rise to 0.1197 pesos in the second quarter compared to 0.092 pesos per share in the second quarter of 1996.
Analysts also expected the operating margin to grow due to various factors, including a decrease in expenses.
"The operating profit will increase due to decreasing expenses, due to their savings," said Esteban Galindez, an analist with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
